installLicensePanel.heading: Four steps. Your prompts never touch our servers.
installLicensePanel.step1: 1 · Get your license key — the SDK is public but fail-closed; it only runs with a valid key. Passed as licenseKey.
installLicensePanel.step2: 2 · Create & verify a service-account key — a machine credential (bvk_…) that does two jobs: it reports counts-only usage (your seats & savings), and it lets the SDK collect your renewed license by itself every billing period. Separate from the license key; only its hash is stored. Create one, then Test my key to confirm it's live.
installLicensePanel.shownOnce: shown once at creation — only the prefix is stored.
installLicensePanel.renewalNote: Keep this key in your deployment. Your license expires at the end of each billing period and the renewal mints a new one. With this key the SDK collects it and swaps it in without a restart. Without it nobody collects it, so someone has to paste the new key by hand every period — and if nobody does, the SDK stops once the grace period ends, even though the subscription is paid and up to date.
installLicensePanel.step3: 3 · Install — public on npm, no token, no config.
installLicensePanel.step4: 4 · Wire your provider & read the SavingsReport
installLicensePanel.gatewayNote: Coding terminal instead of an app? The same package ships a local measuring gateway: bvsala claude launches Claude Code through it and this dashboard shows the spend, token by token. Also bvsala codex, bvsala goose and bvsala qwen; bvsala doctor prints the exact block for the rest. It uses the same service key from step 2 — measuring needs no license key.
installLicensePanel.finalNote: That's it. No valid license → generate() refuses. If your plan is cancelled the SDK stops within ~15 min via licenseServerUrl — no restart, and it never bricks your production if we're unreachable.

cascade.title: Cheapest execution wins

steps.title: Compress what remains
steps.sub: leaner encoding · only when it pays off

cascade.footnote: Each step falls into ONE different ledger, so these figures do not add up to each other. A step whose ledger does not clear zero does not appear here: output restriction was measured and does not save, so it is not advertised.

step2.eyebrow: Step 2 · How savings are measured — reproducible
step2.title: Both arms metered by the provider's own tokenizer — no modeled baseline.
step2.body: This is the output of the A/B benchmark (pnpm ab): for every scenario it sends a naive request and the BV‑SALA request to the same model, prices both from the provider's own token usage, and reports the 95% confidence lower bound — never the flattering point estimate. Nothing is modeled.

anthropicCache.title: Anthropic doesn't cache on its own. Your integration doesn't ask; ours does.
anthropicCache.body: OpenAI applies its prefix cache automatically: you get that discount with us or without us. Anthropic doesn't. It requires marking the cut-off point on every request, and whoever doesn't mark it pays for the whole input, every time.
anthropicCache.evidenceLede: An agent turn with long, repeated system context — a support assistant, a document extractor. Eight pairs, same model in both arms, priced with Anthropic's own counter.
anthropicCache.figureNote: less cost on those requests · 95% lower bound at 78.0% · quality 8/8, no regression
anthropicCache.scopeTitle: What this number does NOT say
anthropicCache.scope: It is the saving of that lever on that traffic, not on your whole bill. It comes from the stable-prefix scenario, where the cache money lives; on traffic without repeated context this lever is worth zero. The headline for the full run is measured separately, and we publish it with its interval, above.
anthropicCache.verifyTitle: And you don't have to take our word for it
anthropicCache.verify: You can check it on your own bill without installing anything: look at whether your Claude calls carry cache_read_input_tokens. If they come back at zero, you are leaving that discount on the table today.

ledgersHead.title: Four separate ledgers. Never summed into one vanity number.
ledgersHead.body: A cache hit removes a whole call. BV‑SALA re‑encodes structured data more compactly. Compression drops redundant words. A provider prefix cache makes tokens cheaper without removing them. Mixing them lies to you — so we don't.
ledgersHead.providerNote: Four ledgers measured against the OpenAI API. A percentage without its model next to it means nothing: the same lever can save on one model and cost on another.

skill.title: The skill that stretches your subscription caps
skill.body: No invoice doesn't mean no pain: the five-hour window and the weekly cap. savings-mode is a pure-instructions skill — no proxy, your traffic untouched — that cuts the two masses that actually burn cap: model output and tool results. It's free; what you pay Savings for is knowing how much it saves you.

skill.mEscrituraDesc: Every tool result is cache-written at a premium before being re-read.

howItWorks.metaTitle: Where does the saving install? · BiVelio Savings Layer
howItWorks.metaDescription: BV‑SALA is a layer that installs in your application's code, where the API is called. What it can save, where it doesn't apply, and how it's truly measured.
howItWorks.title: Where does the saving install?
howItWorks.lede: BV‑SALA is not an app, not an extension, not a ChatGPT setting. It's a piece of code a developer places inside their own application, right where that application calls the OpenAI or Anthropic API. It can only save where a per-token bill exists — and can only measure it where it sees every request go by.
howItWorks.s1Title: The layer lives inside your code
howItWorks.s1Sub: The same call, with and without the layer. Traffic always travels straight from your application to the provider — BV‑SALA is not a middleman server and never sees your data from outside.
howItWorks.nodeLayerSub: avoids calls · trims input and output
howItWorks.s1Note: That green box is an npm package inside the application's code. That's why the key question is never “what do I install?” but “who wrote the code that calls the API?” — that person is who can install it. The one exception is a coding terminal like Claude Code: there the “bvsala claude” gateway sits in front without touching a single line of code.
howItWorks.s2Sub: Four ways of using AI, and what BV‑SALA can do in each one.
howItWorks.caseChatSub: app or web, free or paid
howItWorks.caseChatBody: You pay a flat fee (or nothing): there is no per-token bill to reduce, and it's a closed product where nobody can place software between the app and its models. BV‑SALA's saving simply doesn't apply here — and no product can honestly promise it there.
howItWorks.caseClaudeBody: Exactly the same case: flat subscription and closed product. Use Claude with peace of mind — there is no token spend to optimize from outside.
howItWorks.caseCodeBody: On a subscription, same as above: flat fee, nothing to install. With an API key there is a real per-token bill — and the meter is live: “bvsala claude” launches Claude Code through the local gateway and your spend shows up in your panel, token by token, without touching a line of code. Saving there is the next phase — first we measure for real.
howItWorks.caseAppBody: The case BV‑SALA exists for. Your app calls the API with your key, the provider bills every token, and the layer installs in three steps: package, license, and wrapping the call. From the first request it returns a SavingsReport with the verified saving.
howItWorks.s3Sub: The product has two different numbers, and they shouldn't be mixed.
howItWorks.mBeforeBody: The calculator in the pricing section projects your savings from your own numbers: requests, tokens and model. It's an honest projection — that's why it carries the “estimate” tag.
howItWorks.mAfterBody: Every call returns a SavingsReport: the calls you never paid for and the net saving per request. Auditable, request by request, on your own infrastructure.
howItWorks.s4Title: The full install, if you build an app
howItWorks.snip3: wrap the call — this is the entire code change
